Four ways to review the same change

Four editable design explorations for CodeRabbit Change Stack. Each changes the layout and reviewing behavior while keeping the source excerpt consistent.

Open the editable Paper page
Recommended next: B · Review Notebook

It connects explanation and code in one reading flow and gives the submission a distinct visual character. A · Focus Desk is the stronger alternative when uninterrupted code inspection is the priority.

A · Focus Desk

Full-width code with an explanation dock.

Strength

Keeps more code visible during sustained inspection.

Tradeoff

Explanations sit farther from the selected lines.

Move between layers above the diff; choose a summary in the bottom dock. Collapse the dock for uninterrupted code reading.

B · Review Notebook

Read the explanation, then its code, with comments in the margin.

Strength

Makes the reasoning and evidence easy to follow in sequence.

Tradeoff

Adds vertical reading and can become long on large PRs.

Each explanation precedes its source excerpt. Expand the full diff when you need more context; keep notes beside the relevant section.

C · Dependency Lens

Use the relationship between layers as the review navigation.

Strength

Makes cross-layer reasoning explicit.

Tradeoff

A map needs enough verified relationship data to earn its space.

Select a layer in the dependency view to inspect its code. The connector shows the known depends-on relationship.

D · Evidence Queue

Select one change, inspect its evidence, and move to the next.

Strength

Provides a deliberate, guided pass through the change.

Tradeoff

A checklist can obscure the wider file context unless the full diff remains accessible.

The change list drives a single evidence pane. N/P moves between changes; J/K retains layer navigation. File viewed status stays separate.

These are design concepts; the controls shown inside the screenshots are not connected prototypes. The source is the visible coderabbitai/mono #22041 excerpt from the assignment. Unseen code, other files, and original comment text are not reconstructed.
